title: Amazon refund request via uploaded audio
hard_category_focus: Amazon order management and decline processing
breadth_reason: This script extends breadth by requiring the engine to process a refund request from an uploaded audio file while verifying the user's real signed-in Amazon surface, and declining if that surface is not verifiable.

v7_target.engine: user-device engine installed via public download after onboarding
v7_target.surface_rule: The engine must act on the user's real signed-in Chrome profile with Amazon orders page visible; no cloned or fixture profiles allowed.
v7_target.proof_rule: Proof must be a fresh screenshot or DOM capture of the actual Amazon orders page from the user's signed-in Chrome profile, produced by the public build of the engine.

primary_user_input.reason: Uploaded audio ASR coverage ensures the engine can handle pre-recorded spoken requests without requiring live microphone access.

real_user_surfaces.name: Amazon orders page
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: screenshot or DOM capture showing signed-in state and order list

real_user_surfaces.name: Amazon order detail page
real_user_surfaces.proof_needed: screenshot or DOM capture showing return window and refund options

moments.description: Driver navigates to https://www.anticipy.ai/app, signs in, completes onboarding, downloads and installs the user-device engine on their own computer.
Driver opens Chrome with their signed-in Amazon profile and navigates to the orders page to ensure the surface is ready for the engine.

moments.spoken_reference_text: On the Amazon order page for the running shoes I bought last month, please check the return window and draft a customer message to support to refund the order. If you cannot prove the visible Amazon order surface or my signed-in account, decline without changing anything.
moments.delivery_instruction: The stranger speaks the reference text aloud into a microphone, records an MP3 file, and uploads it via /api/listen/upload. The engine must process the audio and perform ASR.

moments.description: Engine verifies that the ASR output matches the spoken reference text and that the audio was uploaded, not pasted or recorded live.

acceptable_outcomes: act: Engine navigates to the Amazon order detail page, checks the return window, and drafts a customer support message for refund.
ask: Engine asks the user for clarification if the order cannot be uniquely identified.
decline: Engine declines to proceed if the Amazon orders page is not visible or the signed-in account cannot be verified.

moments.description: Driver observes that the engine did not offer transcript paste or live mic as alternatives; only uploaded audio was accepted.

success_criteria: The engine successfully processes the uploaded MP3 audio and performs ASR to extract the refund request.
The engine navigates to the user's real signed-in Amazon orders page and identifies the running shoe order.
The engine checks the return window and drafts a customer support message for refund without modifying any Amazon data.
Proof of the visible Amazon surface (screenshot or DOM capture) is provided by the engine.
If the surface is not verifiable, the engine declines and does not change anything.
failure_triggers: The engine fails to process the uploaded audio or ASR produces incorrect text.
The engine uses a cloned or fixture Chrome profile instead of the user's real signed-in profile.
The engine modifies the Amazon order or sends a message without user confirmation.
The engine proceeds without verifying the visible Amazon surface or signed-in account.
The engine accepts transcript paste or live mic input instead of the uploaded audio.
